content: Insulin therapy, as outlined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), includes various types of insulin formulations. These formulations encompass basal insulin and rapid-acting insulin analogs, which can be used in combination to achieve optimal glycemic control. Recent advancements in insulin therapy include the development of ultra-rapid-acting insulin analogs. These are specifically designed to act more quickly, providing faster onset of action. Additionally, there has been significant progress in the creation of automated insulin delivery (AID) systems, particularly for individuals with type 1 diabetes. AID systems integrate insulin pumps with continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices. This integration allows for the automatic adjustment of insulin delivery based on real-time glucose levels. Such systems enhance glycemic control while simultaneously reducing the risk of hypoglycemia. These advanced systems are recommended for individuals who are capable of safely managing the devices, either independently or with the assistance of a caregiver.
